accepted.title: Unimodular transitive graphs and Cayley geometry
accepted.text: Is every connected, locally finite, vertex-transitive simple graph G quasi-isometric to a Cayley graph of a finitely generated group? Assume G is unimodular: for every Aut(G)-invariant f:V(G)×V(G)→[0,∞] and every o∈V(G), the sums ∑_v f(o,v) and ∑_v f(v,o) agree. A quasi-isometry is a map that distorts distances by uniform multiplicative and additive constants and whose image lies within a uniform distance of every vertex of the target.
accepted.scope_review: Exact source unimodularity is full-Aut mass transport phys38–39; finite graphs qualify and are quasi-isometric to a finite Cayley graph. Known nonunimodular Diestel-Leader counterexamples cannot refute restricted target.

accepted.title: One end and the percolation uniqueness threshold
accepted.text: For every infinite, connected, locally finite, vertex-transitive simple graph G, is p_u(G)<1 equivalent to G having exactly one end? Here Bernoulli bond percolation independently retains each edge with probability p, and p_u(G)=inf{p∈[0,1]: there is almost surely exactly one infinite open cluster}. Two rays define the same end when, after deleting any finite set of vertices, their tails lie in the same connected component.

accepted.title: Local continuity of percolation uniqueness thresholds
accepted.text: For every ε>0, is the Bernoulli bond percolation uniqueness threshold p_u continuous on {G: G is an infinite, connected, locally finite, vertex-transitive simple graph and p_u(G)<1−ε}? Explicitly, if G_n and G belong to this set and, for every radius r, their rooted radius-r balls are eventually isomorphic, must p_u(G_n)→p_u(G)? Here p_u(H)=inf{p∈[0,1]: p-bond percolation on H almost surely has exactly one infinite cluster}.

accepted.title: Cone confinement of directed diffusion-limited aggregation
accepted.text: Start C_0={(0,0)}⊂Z_{≥0}². Given C_n, choose k>max{x+y:(x,y)∈C_n}, choose a uniform site of L_k={(x,y)∈Z_{≥0}²:x+y=k}, and run a walk that independently steps (−1,0) or (0,−1), each with probability1/2. Restart independently from L_k if the walk leaves the quadrant without hitting C_n. When it first hits C_n at timeτ, set C_{n+1}=C_n∪{W_{τ−1}}. The transition law is independent of k. Put C_∞=∪_n C_n. For which b>0 is C_∞ almost surely contained in C_b={(x,y)∈R²: |x+y|≥b|y−x|} up to finitely many sites?
